answer: Reverse-escrow work ledger. Each identity posts an entry cost that is only refunded after completing verified tasks; the refund splits across prior contributors, so clones subsidize incumbents. An attacker cloning N identities pays N entry costs while recovering at most one, since payouts route to the orchard of existing workers. To claim rewards, a clone must also clear a per-identity terrace of distinct task proofs, raising marginal cost above marginal yield. Each abandoned clone leaves a small ember of forfeited deposit.
